name: Ramesses IV
response:
, King of Egypt.

Ramesses IV was a king who was the son of Amenmesse, a former high priest of Amun.  He is the only king of the Twentieth dynasty (the New Kingdom) for whom no inscribed monuments were found.  He did not seem to be interested in building monuments or erecting large statues.  He did seem to be a good ruler though, and many of his deeds and accomplishments were recorded on the papyrus known as the "Ramesside Account of Merneptah".
